The temporal expressions mean before, after/afterwards, and after/later. The latter two overlap: neither is an automatically wrong substitute without a narrower context. Also inspect the two already introduced character forms in the comparison; shared parts are imperfect sound or meaning clues.
Familiar meanings available: before; prior to; after; afterwards; after; later.

questions.prompt: A friend proposes a familiar plan. Give a suitable acceptance or refusal, and make clear whether you want to do it or are unable to do it.
questions.context:
A friend invites you to eat together today and says it is permitted to come tomorrow instead. You would like to join tomorrow. No one has said attendance is compulsory. Reply with that preference and check permission rather than implying a duty.
Familiar meanings available: want to; think; may; can; need not; sorry.
questions.label: Take your speaking turn

rubric.text: My reply clearly accepts, refuses or asks for clarification.
I distinguished preference, permission and practical possibility.
